---
slug: a_fateful_date
title: A Fateful Date
blurb: Sanya lays out a hunter's feast in a glowing blue fern grove for a night alone with Mary, but her Floran urges and an unfamiliar feeling complicate the evening.
authors: Brody
season: FF3
format: prose
---

Sanya found herself standing alone. The air was damp, and while there was no sunlight here, the leaves on the ferns glowed a vibrant blue with luminescence. The plants were a dark, navy blue, nearly black. As Sanya prepped the area, she checked her wristpad, making sure she had the right coordinates. She had managed to procure some time alone from the Pummelers under the guise of “Traditional Floral Training,” which wasn’t inherently untrue. Her Urges had begun to grow, as she hadn’t been able to fully hunt in a while. The last attempt went, well…

Sanya shuddered, attempting to relinquish her mind’s grip on the images of what Seth did to that beast. Disgusting. Steadying herself against a large, glowing green mushroom, Sanya took stock of the food she had brought for the night. Large hunks of traditional Fabriek Cattle (while many small planets of the Fabriek System processed Cattle, Sanya had always had a favorite of Orbitor #6), haunches from members of a Tabaxi-run, planet-wide smuggling ring, and assorted fleshes of rare and standard races. It’s been GUYs since Sanya went all out splurging on food, but Mary told her that they should enjoy this night to the best they could. And due to this, Sanya had even gone out of her way to procure assorted cheeses, breads, wines, and fruits.

[*What happened to you, hunter? When did you put down the spear and pelts for the garb of the lover?*]{Dread}

“[Silence yourself. Tonight is not for you.]{Sanya Dreadflower}”

[*You feel it, don’t you? The necessity to prey on anything, EVERYTHING.*]{Dread}

Sanya ignored the flower. This night was to be enjoyed between two friends. Simply that. After all, the two had become closer after the nights spent studying the Temple, so why shouldn’t they spend some time outside of the temple? It was natural. Just as natural as the urges, pulsing through her body. But, this feeling, deep in her abdomen…

“[Red! There you are! I’ve been scouring the sector for you!]{Mary}”

It’s impossible to describe the feeling that triggered inside Sanya. At least, it would be impossible for HER to describe it. From the outside perspective, it would be easy to assume that a mix of Floran Urges mixed with the swell of Butterflies in someone's stomach combined to mix a horrendously mismatched feeling. It would also be apparent, from the outside, that Sanya acted immediately and unconsciously of those feelings. For with a snarl and a pounce, Sanya had pinned Mary to the floor on first sight, gripping her wrists against the soily ground.

[*Stop this, stop this now, pull back, apologize, end this now, save her, protect her.*]{Sanya Dreadflower}

[*Continue, consume her, devour her, make her yours, your love, your meal, your prey.*]{Dread}

Sanya didn’t move. She remained in the position, towering over Mary, holding her to the ground. The scent of the food Sanya had brought seemed to entwine with the scent of Mary’s…

No. This wasn’t Fear, not fully. It was there, yes, but not the primary emotion in the air. It was a scent unknown to Sanya, a concoction of fear and… excitement? Was Mary… excited by this? Focusing on her face, Sanya could recognize the fear, yes, but the scent, the excitement, it was there too. And then, as their eyes met, Sanya could tell what it was. Trust. Mary wasn’t afraid for her life, no, for she believed Sanya would cause no true harm. None that couldn’t be fixed. Their eyes remained locked, a smile of expectation on Mary’s face.

“[Come now, Red. I know this wasn’t a trap to kill me, you would have done that long ago. And being this forward, while enjoyable, seems FAR too out of character for the strong, stoic Red I know. So, what’s really happening?]{Mary}”

Sanya struggled to relinquish her primal grip on the other, battling her very nature not to consume the Angeli. She turned to focus on the stench of the cattle, and just as quick as she was on top of Mary, she began devouring the hunk of flesh. Blood still coursing down her maw, she turned her face, unspeaking, back towards Mary.

“[Red? I can’t help you if you won’t talk to me.]{Mary}”

The floran turned, crouched down on all fours, and circled the container of produce. She gestured to it, as if to offer some to her guest. Approaching the container, Mary gazed upon the food Sanya had brought tonight.

“[I’m guessing you got just a bit too hungry. I must have made you wait too long, I’m so sorry. And after you went out of your way to get me some too!]{Mary}”

Kneeling down, Mary grabbed the glass cube of wine, sliding the top open with a flick of the hand. Grabbing a small knife, the Angeli cut a few slices of bread and cheese, and sat next to the cooler. Sanya continued to slink around, keeping distance at first, but coming closer at the beckoning of Mary.

“[You don't have to stay over there, Red. I trust you, you can come closer.]{Mary}”

Upon Sanya’s approach, Mary took note of the mental distance Sanya showcased. Still avoiding her touch and gaze, still distancing herself to maintain safety. It wasn’t until Sanya finished another haunch that Mary closed that distance. Wiping some of the blood away from her fangs, the Angeli gave a warm smile.

“[You don’t trust you, do you?]{Mary}”

“[Don't Understand This Mix Of Feelings.]{Sanya Dreadflower}”

“[What feelings, Red? You can talk to me.]{Mary}”

“[The Need To Hunt. To Prey On Weak. To Consume. And… And This Want. This Want Of… Of You.]{Sanya Dreadflower}”

Mary couldn’t help but laugh at the Floran, now inches from her face.

“[I’m so sorry! I- I- I know I shouldn’t be laughing, but I- but I- hahah! Oooh, Red, I can’t believe you. Stoic every time I look at you, and yet, you can’t tell if you’re happy or sad.]{Mary}”

Sanya tilted her head, unaware of the point Mary was trying to make.

“[It’s alright, Red. I understand. You’re experiencing Love. Or, a weird obsession with your food. But for my sake, I’ll hope it's love.]{Mary}”

“[Love?]{Sanya Dreadflower}”

“[That feeling, deep in your stomach, that you get when you look at someone. The smile that comes to your face when you think about them. The happiness you feel when you spend time together, or the anxiousness you feel when you’re apart. Love, Sanya.]{Mary}”

And as Mary looked at Sanya, she couldn’t help but smile. It was strange and chaotic, birthed from a murder spree, and cultivated in a lifeless desert. But Mary knew what this feeling was. What she was feeling. What Sanya was feeling.

Mary took Sanya’s hand in her own. Wiping the last of the blood off of the Floran's face, Mary gave that warm smile with those cunning, starry eyes. She pulled herself closer to Sanya, and as she closed her eyes, the floran closed hers as well.

And the night was theirs, and theirs alone.
